sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill in Sarasota County, FL?
sections.html:
The Sarasota County Tax Collector sends the bill and takes the payment, while the Sarasota County Property Appraiser sets the value and decides exemptions. Neither office sets the tax rate, which comes from the county, the school board, the cities and other taxing districts.

The collector's website says the real estate bill is one combined notice of ad valorem taxes and non-ad valorem assessments such as fire protection and solid waste. A tangible personal property bill is ad valorem only. Ask the tax collector for a copy if your bill does not arrive; the office says to tell it if nothing has come by November 15.

Four municipalities sit inside the county and are linked from the collector's site: Sarasota, North Port, Venice and Longboat Key. The collector also lists office locations in downtown Sarasota, Venice, North Port and Mid County. For a house in town, see our pages on selling in Sarasota, North Port and Venice.

sections.h2: When are Sarasota County property taxes due and when do they go delinquent?
sections.html:
Bills are payable starting November 1, and unpaid tax becomes delinquent on April 1 of the following year. The collector's example: unpaid 2025 taxes turned delinquent on April 1, 2026.

Paying early earns a discount. The collector prints 4 percent for November, 3 percent for December, 2 percent for January and 1 percent for February, with the gross amount due by March 31. A mortgage servicer that pays from escrow must pay inside the 4 percent window, according to the same page.

The 2026 bills were mailed or emailed by October 30, and the Property Appraiser certified the 2026 roll to the collector on September 29, 2026. Statewide, taxpayers who cannot pay in a lump sum can apply to the tax collector for an installment plan by May 1 of the assessment year, and a homestead owner can file Form DR-570 for a deferral by March 31.

sections.h2: How do you challenge your Sarasota County assessment?
sections.html:
Start by calling or meeting the Property Appraiser's staff, then file a petition with the Value Adjustment Board if the concern is not settled. The appraiser's page says you may skip the informal step and go straight to the board or even to circuit court.

The petition deadline is 25 days after the TRIM notice is mailed, and the date is printed on the notice. For a denied exemption or a denied transfer of an assessment difference, the window is 30 days from the date the denial letter was mailed. The Clerk to the Value Adjustment Board handles filing questions at (941) 861-5279, and electronic filing is available.

If you still disagree with the board, the appraiser's page says a claim may be filed in circuit court within 60 days of the roll being certified. The board hears challenges to value, classification and exemptions only. A complaint about the tax rate goes to the individual taxing authority, and you can speak at the budget hearings listed on your notice.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can lower a Sarasota County bill?
sections.html:
Homestead is the main one, and you must own and occupy the home as your permanent residence on January 1 and apply by March 1. The appraiser's office says it will still consider late applications.

Florida's Department of Revenue describes the homestead exemption as up to $50,000, with the first $25,000 applying to all taxes including school taxes. After the first year, Save Our Homes limits assessment growth to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change. The appraiser's overview also lists these personal exemptions for Florida permanent residents:

  • Widow or widower exemption of $5,000, ended by remarriage.
  • Disability exemption of $5,000 for total and permanent disability.
  • Blind person exemption of $5,000.
  • Disabled veteran exemption of $5,000 for a service-connected rating of at least 10 percent.
  • A veteran aged 65 or older with a permanent combat-related disability may receive a homestead discount equal to the VA percentage.

The Sarasota County Tax Collector's site notes that voter-approved Amendment 3 changes will affect the 2027 bill, not the 2026 bill. Ask the Property Appraiser how the new rules apply to your parcel.

sections.h2: What happens if Sarasota County property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
The tax collector sells a tax certificate on the unpaid amount, and a certificate holder can later apply for a tax deed. The collector's own page warns that failure to pay can result in the loss of the property.

Florida's Department of Revenue says certificates are sold on all unpaid items by June 1. Under s. 197.432, the bidder who accepts the lowest interest rate wins, in quarter-percent steps. A holder may apply for a tax deed after two years have run since April 1 of the issue year, and the application fee is $75 under s. 197.502. At the clerk's sale, the high bidder posts a nonrefundable deposit of 5 percent of the bid or $200, whichever is greater, under s. 197.542.

A seller who is behind on tax can settle the balance through closing, and the closing agent asks the collector for the amount owed. The sooner you act, the fewer months of delinquency apply.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about property tax when closing in Sarasota County?
sections.html:
The buyer owes the full year's bill to the collector, and the seller's share is settled between the two on the closing statement. The tax collector states that no part is paid to its office as a partial payment by the seller.

Because bills go to the owner of record, tell the Property Appraiser your new mailing address after you sell. The collector also asks sellers who get a bill for a house they no longer own to forward it to the new owner or return it to the collector. A tangible property bill is different: if you owned business property on January 1, you still owe that year's tax.

Our Sarasota County property records guide covers the recording side, including deed stamps.

sections.h2: How do you reach the Sarasota County tax offices?
sections.html:
The Property Appraiser is at 2001 Adams Lane, Sarasota, FL 34237, and takes calls at 941.861.8200. Use that office for value, exemption and mailing address questions; the tax collector handles bills and payments.

Bring these items to a conference with the appraiser's staff or a hearing before the board:

  • Your TRIM notice and parcel number.
  • Recent sales of similar houses nearby.
  • Repair estimates or photos if damage lowers the value.
  • Proof of residency papers if an exemption was denied.

The appraiser says issues are often settled in informal talks, so a short call before the petition deadline can save a filing.

faqs.q: When is Sarasota County property tax due?
faqs.a: Bills are payable from November 1 and become delinquent on April 1 of the next year. Discounts run 4 percent in November, 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Sarasota County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Sarasota County Tax Collector, through the payment options listed on its website, or at one of its offices in downtown Sarasota, Venice, North Port or Mid County.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Sarasota County property value?
faqs.a: Yes. File a petition with the Value Adjustment Board within 25 days of the TRIM notice mailing, as printed on your notice. Denied exemptions have a 30-day window from the denial letter.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or seller pay the tax bill at closing?
faqs.a: The buyer is responsible for the whole bill to the collector. The seller's share for the months of ownership is credited on the closing statement.

faqs.q: What if I cannot pay my Sarasota County taxes?
faqs.a: Ask the tax collector about an installment plan, which must be applied for by May 1 of the assessment year, or about a homestead deferral using Form DR-570 by March 31. Unpaid tax can end in a tax certificate and a tax deed.
